beats.text: This circular hole is three hundred eighteen meters wide, and no one dug it.
So what carved this giant marine sinkhole?
Jacques Cousteau called it one of the top five scuba sites worldwide.
From orbit the hole appears as a perfect circle on the reef.
It is one hundred twenty four meters deep.
During the Quaternary sea levels fell, dissolving limestone and forming a cavity.
When seas rose again, the cavity flooded, creating the water-filled hole.
Today divers explore its ledges, finding ancient stalactites at twenty one meters.
Next target: a crater once larger than Chicxulub. Follow for the next scan. Orbi out.

draft.description: The Great Blue Hole is a three hundred eighteen meter wide marine sinkhole off Belize, formed when sea levels fell during the Quaternary. Jacques Cousteau made it famous as a top scuba diving site.
